extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, critics, and practitioners of comic literature and drama (playwrights, essayists, literary critics)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying criteria for creating and evaluating 'pure Comedy' and related comic modes (satire, irony, humour) across plays, novels, and poems; aimed at critics, students, and writers of comic literature. Focuses on what makes comedy succeed conceptually and socially rather than on technical stagecraft alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: The life of comedy is the idea
rubrics_metrics.description: The vitality of a comedy rests not on elaborate plot mechanics but on a central comedic idea — 'The life of the comedy is in the idea.' One must 'love pure Comedy warmly' and be receptive to the Comic idea to understand great works like The Misanthrope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize a strong conceit or intellectual principle that animates the whole piece; thin or merely contrived plots are acceptable only when they serve a potent comic idea. Example: Molière's Misanthrope relies on an idea (conflict of worldliness vs unworldliness) rather than plot complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the real world and human nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy requires accurate knowledge of the real world and of men and women 'well enough not to expect too much of them' while retaining hope for good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground comic types and situations in believable human behaviour; idealization is permitted but should be founded on recognizable reality. Avoid caricature that sacrifices truth for mere effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social conditions for pure Comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Pure Comedy flourishes only where society exists with some equality and freedom between the sexes; where women have social freedom and are not reduced to drudgery, the Comic Muse can be transplanted from life to stage or novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating works or cultures, consider whether social structures permit the kinds of social interaction and dialogue that Comedy depends on (e.g., contrast with societies where the veil or sex-separation precludes comic social life).

rubrics_metrics.name: The Comic is perceptive, not contemptuous
rubrics_metrics.description: Comic perception is incompatible with contempt; contempt or anger is a failure of comic intelligence and closes off humane understanding of Folly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid a disdainful attitude toward comedic subjects. The comic voice should be observing and discerning rather than simply scornful or enraged; laughter should come from insight, not moral hauteur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attack Folly with the Comic's lightness and swiftness
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy is the specific remedy for Folly; it should strike early, lightly, and unweariedly so that Folly has no time to entrench or seduce the multitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer nimble, perceptive comic exposure to long defensive essays or heavy-handed refutation. Antipattern: long, ponderous invective gives Folly time to form 'entrenchments.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish Comic from Satire, Irony, and Humour
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comic is distinct from related modes: Satire is a moral agent (a social scavenger working on bile), Irony is often the humour of satire (can be savage or sedate), and Humour embraces contrasts and may comfort the feelings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When crafting or judging a piece, identify which mode predominates and whether it suits the work's aims. A truly comic scene addresses the intellect and perceptive faculties rather than merely to satirize or to console.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mere joking and cheap punning
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comic differs from jokers and from humour that relies on punning or 'humouristic phrase'; such tricks blunt the sense of the Comic and require training of the audience's wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate linguistic devices: excessive polysyllabic jesting or routine puns indicate humouristic leisure but can blunt comic perception. True comedy addresses the wits and elicits an intellectual laughter, not only a mechanical chuckle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the audience share characters' delusions to enable the comic turn
rubrics_metrics.description: Masterstrokes of comedy secure the audience's sympathy with a character's prepossession (e.g., Orgon's 'Le pauvre homme!' for Tartuffe), so that when the turn comes the comic reversal is powerful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build comic scenes that invite the audience into the character's belief long enough to feel the contrast at the reveal; the humour depends on shared perception and then on the sharp turn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use idealization to create enduring comic types
rubrics_metrics.description: Great comic poets 'idealized upon life' to create principal types—e.g., Tartuffe as father of hypocrites, Sganarelle and Arnolphe as recurring comic figures—grounded in reality but painted with 'spiritual strength.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating comic characters, abstract and amplify features into recognizable types that can be reused across works; the foundation should remain true to common human traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance grotesque/outline comedy with the 'idea' of Comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: National or stylistic tendencies toward sharp outline, quick movement, or grotesque (Spanish, Italian, German examples) can produce lively pieces but risk missing the 'true idea of Comedy' if they devolve into marionette-like action or pure farce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid letting brisk plot or grotesque caricature substitute for the comic idea. Evaluate whether movement/outline serves an intellectual comic concept rather than merely spectacle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic requires training of perception and quickness of wit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comic addresses the wits for laughter; sluggish or untrained wits fail to respond, especially in emotionally charged situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess audience or reader capability: successful comedy often presumes a degree of cultivated perception. Writers should craft signals that can be picked up by attentive, witty audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Comic tolerates and forgives through recognition of likeness
rubrics_metrics.description: True Comic spirit allows one to detect ridicule of those you love without loving them less and to see oneself as somewhat ridiculous in others' eyes; failing this lapses into Satire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good comic effect mixes exposure with affection: it spares and pities while exposing. Evaluate whether comedic treatment preserves humane regard for its characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use contrast and juxtaposition to produce comic insight
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy often arises from the contrast between characters' natures (e.g., Don Quixote and Sancho) or between characters and the wiser society; juxtaposition yields perception and laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct scenes and character pairings that emphasize oppositions to illuminate folly and produce comic understanding rather than mere ridicule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic poet's instrument: common-sense
rubrics_metrics.description: A fundamental quality for comic creation is 'common-sense'—the Comic poet's gift—which guides perception and gives the comic its practical moral compass (distinct from mere political intelligence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value lucidity and practical insight in comic writing; over-intellectualizing or excessive abstruseness undercuts the Comic's effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-level humour may fuse Tragic and Comic elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The great humourist can embrace contrasts beyond the purely comic: humour may fuse the Tragic sentiment with Comic narrative (e.g., Don Quixote), producing a broader, more affecting laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't force comedy to be unemotional; evaluate how tragic light or poignancy is integrated to enrich rather than dilute comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Comic should act as a public corrective to sentimentality and delusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy functions as an auxiliary to common-sense, countering Sentimentalism and public delusion by exposing folly and cutting off its popular appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a comic work successfully undercuts sentimental or delusive currents in society with wit and perception rather than vindictiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate political scope and licence
rubrics_metrics.description: Political comedy can be a forceful instrument (Aristophanes example) but carries social risk; the comic must adapt method and licence to audience and historical circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating political comedy, consider whether its satire is fit for its audience and whether it wields laughter responsibly (recognizing possible consequences like censorship or social backlash).
